text.title: 地图上一排树
text.situation:
下一张地图标记栖息地，不是步道。林地中有该地区原生植物。一张照片展示濒危动物；露丝解释本地罕见与濒危是不同判断。保护计划旨在保护整个地方。保留说明要求工人留下老树篱。砍树可能让筑巢点消失，而毁林描述更大规模森林损失。

乔：会砍这棵树来拓宽小径吗？
露丝：先看谁在利用它，有哪些替代方案。
玛雅：所以保护包括动物住的地方？
露丝：是的，受到保护的动物仍需要栖息地。

paragraphs.en: The next map marked habitats rather than walking routes. A woodland patch held plants indigenous to the region. One photograph showed an endangered animal; Ruth explained that being rare locally and being endangered were different claims. The conservation plan aimed to protect the whole site. A note about preservation asked workers to leave an old hedge in place. Cutting down a tree could remove a nesting place, while deforestation described forest loss on a much larger scale.

paragraphs.en:
Jo: Would you cut down this tree to widen the path?
Ruth: First we would examine what uses it and what alternatives there are.
Maya: So conservation includes the places animals live?
Ruth: Yes. A protected animal still needs a habitat.
